display_name: Five items in the Economic Competition Law, 5748-1988, and the instruments under it, recorded as typed values with their tests: the old name in printed titles (a record), a fee item that cites a repealed section, a fee item whose section no longer holds the application it names, a recital whose two index years are two years apart, and a regulation made under a power in a repealed Law, with one sound control for each; not an encoding of the Law
domain_expert_review: none: no domain expert has read this against the source
seat: the applicant who files a request or an appeal with the Competition Tribunal and pays the fee that the regulations set. The row asks no question from the seat because it records references, titles and a recital.

source.note: all four deposits are excerpts of unofficial consolidations; a reading is CONSOLIDATION-ONLY unless NOTES.md says it was read from a cropped page image of the instrument. The official pages read are cropped images in amending-laws/ and official/; no PDF is deposited.

expected_red.note: two assertions for each of four items, each stating what the printed words need. Item 2: fee item (a)(3) names section 28, which the consolidation prints as repealed. Item 3: fee item (b)(5) names an application under section 30, which holds no application of that kind. Item 4: the recital of Kovetz HaTakanot 11002 p. 948 prints two index years two years apart (the control, Kovetz HaTakanot 10454 p. 598, prints them one year apart). Item 5: the 1964 regulations name a power in the 1959 Law, which the consolidation prints as repealed. Item 1, the old name in printed titles, is a record and has no red assertion.

run.method: one Sonnet builder, from a written brief; the cropped images named in NOTES.md were looked at by the builder
